record.paper_title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems
record.context_brief: Max-min models for nonclassical Jacobi zeros
record.original_question: For Jacobi polynomials with nonclassical real parameters α and β, can the max-min characterization from Theorem 1 be extended after suitably modifying the admissible family F of continua so that the zeros are still characterized by an extremal problem even in regimes with nonhermitian, multiple, or otherwise nonclassical orthogonality and possibly complex zeros?

evidence.quote: We conjecture that Theorem 1 is valid in all these situations after a suitable modification of the family of continua F.
All these facts have been conjectured by one of this authors some time ago, but their proof still remains an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. For real parameters α, β > −1, the classical Jacobi polynomial P_n^{(α,β)} has n simple zeros in (−1,1), and these zeros admit a max–min characterization of the following type. Let F denote a suitable family of continua (compact connected subsets of the complex plane) joining −1 and +1, and for K ∈ F let cap_w(K) denote the weighted logarithmic capacity associated with the external field induced by the Jacobi weight w(x)=(1−x)^α(1+x)^β. Then the zero set of P_n^{(α,β)} (more precisely, the support of the normalized zero-counting measure in an appropriate asymptotic sense) is characterized by an extremal problem of max–min type over F: there exists K* ∈ F maximizing a minimal weighted-energy/capacity functional, and the zeros (or their limit distribution) live on K*.

Problem. Extend this max–min characterization to Jacobi polynomials P_n^{(α,β)} with nonclassical real parameters α, β (e.g. parameters outside (−1, ∞) in which standard orthogonality on [−1,1] fails, so that orthogonality must be replaced by non-Hermitian orthogonality on contours, multiple orthogonality, or another nonclassical variant, and the zeros may be complex). Specifically, determine whether one can modify the admissible family F of continua so that the zeros of P_n^{(α,β)} (or the support of their asymptotic zero distribution) are again characterized as the extremal continuum of a max–min problem of the same type, for all such nonclassical regimes of (α,β). Either prove such a characterization with an explicit description of the modified family F, or exhibit an obstruction.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a published proof of a general max–min characterization for zeros of Jacobi polynomials in the full nonclassical-parameter regime (non-Hermitian/multiple orthogonality, complex zeros). Related partial work exists on pseudo-Jacobi polynomials, extreme zeros, and non-Hermitian orthogonality and S-curves, but a unified extremal-continuum characterization in the spirit asked appears not to be established in the located literature.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonality and asymptotics of Pseudo-Jacobi polynomials for non-classical parameters
status_evidence.snippet: Studies orthogonality and zero asymptotics of Jacobi-type polynomials for nonclassical parameters, but does not establish a general max–min extremal-continuum characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists on nonclassical Jacobi-type zero asymptotics, without proving the general max–min characterization.

status_evidence.title: On the Extreme Zeros of Jacobi Polynomials (Nikolov)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies extreme zeros of classical Jacobi polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Available results address extreme zeros in classical regimes, not the conjectured extension to nonclassical parameter regimes.
